summary: Full text of the 2020 J Sport Health Sci meta-analysis (13 RCTs, 206 adults, acute citrulline malate 6-12 g or citrulline in watermelon juice) shows lower post-exercise RPE (ES 0.81, p=0.03) and 24-h soreness (ES 0.99, p=0.04), with no effect at 48-72 h or on lactate. It gets one eligible context under the record's Increase Energy/exercise-recovery claim. The BP meta-analysis (abstract only) is null and the erectile-function pilot is a citrulline+resveratrol combination, so neither gets credit. The new applicability block covers acute exercise exertion only, not Cardiovascular/Heart Health.

applicability.studied_population: Healthy, mostly trained young adults given a single acute dose of citrulline malate (6-12 g) or citrulline in watermelon juice before exercise; post-exercise RPE and 24-h soreness fell, lactate did not.

identity.preparation: Acute citrulline malate (9 trials, mostly 8 g) or L-citrulline delivered in watermelon juice (4 trials, 1.17-6 g citrulline), within 2 h before exercise.

population.description: 13 RCTs, 206 healthy adults (mostly resistance-trained or recreationally trained young men; some women; amateur runners), aged about 21-35.

study_contexts.study_design: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of randomized (11 double-blind, 2 single-blind) placebo-controlled trials of acute citrulline within 2 h before exercise; primary outcomes RPE and muscle soreness, secondary blood lactate.

dose.administration_frequency: Single acute dose 40 min to 2 h before exercise (Table 1).
dose.reported_regimen: Citrulline malate 6-12 g (8 g in 9 trials) 40-60 min before exercise; L-citrulline 1.17-6 g in watermelon juice 1-2 h before exercise (Table 1). Single acute exposures; no chronic regimen.
co_therapies: Participants generally avoided vigorous exercise, supplements, alcohol and caffeine before sessions; 2 studies allowed usual supplements. Malate is co-delivered in citrulline-malate arms; watermelon juice is a food matrix.

source_provenance.location: Full text (PMC7749242): Methods (eligibility, extraction), Table 1 (13 studies, supplement protocol), Results risk of bias and meta-analysis paragraphs (Figs 2-4), Discussion; reference list 2-14.

outcomes.name: Post-exercise RPE (primary): effect size 0.81, p=0.03, 7 studies, I2 81.9%; still p=0.05 after removing an influential study.
Muscle soreness (primary): 24 h effect size 0.99, p=0.04 (7 studies, I2 92.1%); 48 h p=0.25 (6 studies); 72 h p=0.62 (4 studies).
Blood lactate (secondary): no significant reduction, p=0.17 (8 studies).

limitations: Small trials (206 participants in 13 studies) with very high heterogeneity for RPE and 24-h soreness; soreness benefit did not persist at 48 or 72 h; none had prespecified protocols.

Most arms used citrulline malate (malate co-exposure; citrulline content per gram not standardized) and 4 used watermelon juice (food matrix); no chronic or capsule-specific regimen established. Dosage forms are not tabulated beyond the vehicle.
Included-study identity from the source reference list: 12 PMIDs; Martinez-Sanchez 2017 (Food Nutr Res) has no PMID in the source and none is invented.

Credit covers acute exercise perceived exertion and short-term soreness only; not nitric-oxide, blood-pressure or general energy claims. Returned A087 'source-content hold' is resolved for this source by full-text verification.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

clinical_review.notes: No credit for the cardiovascular claim: the abstract reports no significant blood-pressure effect, and the full text (not open access) was not retrieved to encode regimens or trials.

source_provenance.location: PubMed abstract (Curr Hypertens Rep 2018; not open access).

limitations: Mirenayat 2018 abstract: 5 interventions; brachial SBP change 0.28 mmHg (-2.87 to 2.31), DBP -1.56 (-4.32 to 1.20), aortic SBP 0.22 and DBP 0.26, all non-significant; authors conclude no beneficial BP effect. This null finding argues against the record's Cardiovascular/Heart Health goal.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

identity.chemical_form: Complete L-citrulline 800 mg plus transresveratrol 300 mg daily study supplement, during continued on-demand PDE5-inhibitor use.

population.description: 20 menwith EDdespiteon-demand PDE5 i, 13 complete crossover.

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover pilot of L-citrulline plus transresveratrol during continued on-demand PDE5-inhibitor treatment; no washout before crossover.

dose.administration_frequency: Once daily after a meal, one complex capsule.
dose.reported_regimen: One daily complex capsule after a meal supplying 800 mg L-citrulline plus 300 mg transresveratrol; 1, 100 mg total study actives, not 1, 100 mg L-citrulline.

normalization.basis: Reported study-material daily dose, not a universal threshold or equivalence to other preparation.

source_provenance.location: Full text (PMC6302103): Methods (study design paragraph, Figure 1 protocol, Main Outcome Measure), Results, funding/COI.

co_therapies: Patients continued on-demand PDE5 inhibitors; active study supplement also contained 300 mg/day transresveratrol.

outcomes.name: SHIM total: active 10.96 +/- 1.21 versus placebo 8.31 +/- 1.23 and baseline 8.32 (both P<.05).
Erection Hardness Score 2.56 vs baseline 2.31 (P=.79) and AMS sexual domain: no significant difference.

limitations: Dose 800 mg is citrulline component of combination, not monotherapy effect.
One calendar month per period, no crossover washout, attrition/PDE5 i cotherapy.

The retained full article does not designate a primary outcome/endpoint; recorded hierarchy not_reported. This is a reporting limitation, not invented primary status or completion of any separate approval.

No credit: a two-ingredient capsule (L-citrulline 800 mg + trans-resveratrol 300 mg) added to on-demand PDE5 inhibitors; erectile function is not this record's claim, and 13 of 20 completed. Periods were 30 days (Figure 1) with no washout.
